text:
Gavin McKenna, the first overall pick last June, is 18 and already has 6 goals and 12 points in 19 games. Seven of those points came on the power play. At 5-on-5 it has been harder: Toronto gets only 39% of expected goals with him on the ice, nearly ten points worse than without him.

That gap showed against Montreal on Nov. 7. Yahoo Sports reported he admitted a "mistake" after being benched in the loss, and The Hockey News ran a piece on what coach Jim Hiller told him in the second intermission under the headline "It Fired Me Up." He scored in that game, then went without a shot in 17 minutes against New Jersey the next night.

His speed is real (97th percentile top speed), his 6 goals on 4.0 expected goals are a bit ahead of his chances, and he sits among the top rookie scorers. For context, forwards taken in the top three since 2005 put up a median 0.55 points a game in their first full season; McKenna is running ahead of that. Our range has him at 36 to 61 points.
headline: McKenna's rookie lesson came on a Saturday
